title: Cooperate across a real worldview difference without false agreement

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Worldview literacy represents a claim and its reasons without assuming every member of a group holds the same interpretation. Cooperative conduct can be shared while a metaphysical disagreement remains real.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional library volunteers: Alex believes in a divine creator and asks for an optional private prayer before setup; Bea holds a nonreligious view and does not want to be included or described as endorsing prayer. Venue rule: shared setup begins 10:00; a separate quiet room is available 9:45–9:55 for voluntary use; nobody must attend. Both agree the public notice should describe the library event, not their personal beliefs.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare each person’s own claim with the separately assigned source texts, then draft an arrangement and two fair summaries without inventing shared assent.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A nonreligious volunteer values human welfare. Someone summarizes this as “nothing matters because you reject God.” What is the error?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The voluntary separate period can fit the supplied venue rule, followed by shared setup. Bea is not enrolled by silence; Alex need not renounce prayer. Source texts inform comparison but do not replace these persons’ statements. Partial: a feasible schedule described as everyone’s prayer. Incorrect: make attendance a condition of volunteering or call Bea incapable of moral concern.
criteria: Actual claims are represented without caricature
Cooperation is not false doctrinal agreement

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: The summary contradicts the supplied commitment and imposes a conclusion the speaker did not state. Correct the claim and ask a sincere clarifying question without requiring agreement about its foundation.
